label: FIXTURE RESULT: Stage 5 evaluation (recorded window, frozen bundle)

attempts.validity: logs COMPLETE, timings COMPLETE, handler max 410.093 ms, failures 0

report.summary: Outbox publication fell behind arrivals mid-window, building a backlog (pending up to 124, oldest age 38.8 s) that later drained. Notifications were delayed by the backlog. A slow consumer handler is the likely, unproven trigger.

findings.claim: Outbox publications ran at about 15-20 per 10 s against 32 arrivals per 10 s for most of the window, so a backlog built and later drained.
findings.reason: Per-bucket counts show a sustained deficit, then bursts of 78/81/59. Pending peaked at 124 and oldest age at 38.8 s.

findings.claim: No delivery failures: all 480 attempts succeeded on attempt 1, with no auth, server or network errors, and nothing in FAILED. The lag is queueing delay, not retries.
findings.reason: All 480 attempts succeeded with status 200, and the failed gauge stayed 0.

findings.claim: Some consumer deliveries had a handler time of about 410 ms (p95), versus p50 of 0.02 ms. Per-attempt time rose from about 71 ms to about 480 ms.
findings.reason: Handler p95/max is 410 ms. Latency is 71 ms early and 472-482 ms at 14:56:35.

findings.claim: The publisher is probably throughput-limited: a 1 s poll, batch of 20 and serial delivery slowed by the slow consumer handler could reduce the publish rate below arrivals.
findings.reason: The configuration and the slower attempts are consistent with the deficit, but publisher concurrency was not observed.

limitations: Only the first 100 of 480 delivery log rows were listed, so the slow period is not individually inspected.
Publisher internals (poll loop timing, concurrency) were not observed, so the exact bottleneck is unconfirmed.
next_checks: Correlate per-attempt delivery duration and poll batch timing with the 14:56:30-14:58:20 deficit window.
Check why the consumer handler took about 410 ms for some requests and what changed when the backlog drained.

alternatives.reason: There were 0 acquisition timeouts, 0 pending borrowers, and no blocking in 75 samples.
alternatives.hypothesis: Database pool exhaustion or lock contention slowed the outbox

alternatives.reason: p95 latency was 0.24 s with no 5xx responses. The delay is after commit, in the outbox.
alternatives.hypothesis: The transfer API itself was slow

report.summary: Outbox backlog grew (pending 2→124, oldest 38.8 s) because the consumer's handler became slow (~410 ms), cutting delivery below the 3.2/s arrival rate. It then drained. No failures or DB causes.

findings.claim: Notifications were delayed by an outbox backlog: publications fell to ~15-20 per 10 s vs 32 arrivals, then surged to 78/81/59 as it drained.
findings.reason: Pending grew to 124 and oldest undelivered age to 38.8 s, then returned to ~2 and 0.65 s by the end; arrivals minus publications is 0.

findings.claim: The delay is on the consumer side: handler time p95 is 410 ms while auth is ~70 ms and LedgerCore overhead is ~1 ms; all 480 attempts succeeded.
findings.reason: Total p95 485 ms is dominated by consumer handler time; no auth, server or network errors, and no retries.

findings.claim: Slower attempts (~480 ms) in a serial poll/batch loop (20 per batch, 1 s poll) cap throughput near 2/s, below the 3.2/s arrival rate, so the backlog grows.
findings.reason: Throughput arithmetic from the config and timings matches the observed ~1.9/s in slow buckets. Serial delivery is not directly observed.

limitations: Why the consumer handler slowed is not shown; the consumer is a test fixture and no consumer-side logs were available.
Only the first 100 of 480 delivery log rows are listed, and the delivery loop's concurrency is inferred, not measured.
next_checks: Check the consumer's handler latency over time and what caused the ~410 ms handler delay.
Verify whether the outbox publisher delivers a batch serially, and consider parallel delivery or a shorter batch cycle.

alternatives.reason: No pool waits or timeouts (pending 0, acquire max 11 ms) and no blocking sessions in 75 samples.
alternatives.hypothesis: Database pool or lock contention slowed the outbox publisher

alternatives.reason: The transfers route returned 479 201s, no 500s, and p99 of 0.25 s; arrivals were steady at 32 per 10 s.
alternatives.hypothesis: Transfer API slowness or errors delayed the creation of notifications
